content: 1. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely, as P-gp inhibitors may reduce the clearance of ondansetron. 2. Ivacaftor raises ondansetron levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. No dosage adjustment is recommended, but caution and monitoring are advised. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 3. Ketoconazole elevates ondansetron levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance. No dosage adjustment is recommended. 4. Lenvatinib and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor ECG closely when co-administering QT-prolonging drugs, as recommended in lenvatinib prescribing information. 5. Letermovir increases ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Leuprolide increases ondansetron toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Levoketoconazole raises ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance. No dosage adjustment is recommended. 8. Lomitapide increases ondansetron levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the ondansetron dose when used concomitantly with lomitapide. 9. Lonafarnib increases ondansetron levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor, and minimal concentration changes in P-gp substrates may lead to serious toxicities. Reduce the dose of P-gp substrates if needed. 10. Lopinavir and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid use in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 11. Lorlatinib decreases ondansetron levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Mavorixafor and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 13. Mavorixafor increases ondansetron levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse effects. 14. Ondansetron increases metformin levels by inhibiting renal transporters (MATE or OCTs) responsible for active renal secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ondansetron and metronidazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with high IV doses of ondansetron (do not exceed 16 mg IV). 16. Mifepristone and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 17. Mitotane decreases ondansetron levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer, and dosage adjustments may be necessary for CYP3A4 substrates. 18.
